newsitem.title: GERMANY: Poland must not be "second-class" NATO member-Kohl.
newsitem.headline: Poland must not be "second-class" NATO member-Kohl.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl told Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Friday that Germany was determined the new countries NATO is taking in would not be "second-class" members.

Kohl also reaffirmed to Kwasniewski, on a two-day unofficial visit, that Polish membership of NATO and the European Union were important German foreign policy goals, government spokesman Peter Hausmann said in a statement.

Kohl briefed Kwasniewski on his meeting with Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday in the German spa town of Baden-Baden, where they discussed Russia's objections to NATO's plans to take in new members from eastern Europe.
"He reaffirmed his view (to Kwasniewski) that there would be no lower-quality membership in the course of NATO expansion," Hausmann said.

Moscow has made clear that it vehemently opposes NATO's expansion in eastern Europe, but Yeltsin said in Baden-Baden that Russia and NATO would sign a charter in May aimed at giving Russia more influence in NATO as it enlarges.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are in the front line of countries expected to be invited to join the alliance at a NATO summit in Madrid in July.

One of Russia's key demands is that NATO agree to limit the stationing of foreign troops and infrastructure in new member states in east Europe. But the aspiring members object that this would make them second class alliance members.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel gave Kwasniewski assurances similar to Kohl's.
"As far as NATO's opening to new members is concerned, it was clear there should and will be no first or second class members," a foreign ministry statement on their meeting said.
"In particular, Russia must be included in European security architecture in accordance with its influence and importance."
